title: How 2.3 Million Blocks Built the Great Pyramid (It Wasn't Slaves)
description:
The Great Pyramid took about 2.3 million stone blocks. So who stacked them, and how? Not whipped slaves, and not aliens. The real answer is a paid, fed, medically cared-for workforce with its own city, and a few tricks that still surprise engineers.

In this video we walk the site step by step:
- Why Hollywood (and a Greek historian called Herodotus) got the "slave" story wrong
- The lost city of the pyramid builders, with bakeries, dormitories and copper workshops
- The crew names painted inside the pyramid: the "Friends of Khufu" and the "Drunkards of Menkaure"
- What the workers actually ate (garlic, onions, bread, beef and thick beer)
- The healed broken bones that prove they got real medical care
- The wet-sand trick that cut the pulling force of a two-ton block roughly in half
- The ramp debate: straight, zig-zag or internal? Nobody knows for sure

Sources and further reading: Mark Lehner's excavations of the Giza workers' town (Lost City of the Pyramids), Herodotus' Histories, and the 2014 sand-wetting experiment by physicists at the University of Amsterdam (Fall et al., Physical Review Letters). Some details are still debated by historians; where that is the case, the video says so.

This video uses an AI-assisted narrator and illustrations.
